title: Split-Rail Cost Comparison Pattern and Interaction Rhythm Audit
creator: Lena Park
description: Problem: The console’s existing cost and rollout surfaces combine dense numeric data with decision UI in ways that reduce scan efficiency and cause inconsistent micro-interactions across breakpoints. Goal: Define a new split-rail card pattern (left: compact summary metrics and quick actions; right: expandable detail, rollouts timeline, and cost-sparkline canvas) and a precise interaction rhythm (timing, easing, and state transitions) so engineers and product teams can implement consistent behavior across console pages. Deliverables: Figma component library additions (SplitRailCard variants, CompactMetric token set), a short interaction spec (timing/easing, focus states, keyboard flows), accessibility checks (screen reader labels and focus order), and a handoff checklist for frontend implementation and QA.
acceptance_criteria: Figma library contains SplitRailCard with three variants: summary-only, summary+expand, and expanded-detail
Token mapping document links all visual properties to token names (color, spacing, elevation, motion-duration) and no hard-coded values remain in master components
Interaction rhythm doc specifies animation durations and easings for enter/exit, expand/collapse, hover affordances, and disabled states
Responsive rules defined: at <=720px the pattern collapses to stacked cards; between 721–1024px it uses a narrow-rail layout; >=1025px shows full split-rail
Accessibility: screen reader order, aria-expanded, and keyboard-only expand/collapse keys documented and validated in a quick audit
Frontend PR implements CSS variable-driven tokens and passes visual regression for three core pages (Cost Overview, Rollouts, Dedicated Capacity).
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose split-rail over popover-heavy pattern for scan efficiency after hallway usability tests (reason: faster metric comparison and fewer context switches)
2026-03-04: Agreed on token-first approach: all spacing and motion values use token names (motion.duration.short/medium/long)
2026-03-07: Determined responsive collapse breakpoint at 720px to align with existing console grid and mobile layout constraints

accessibility_notes: Ensure aria-expanded present on toggle and label includes current ratio (eg. 'Expand cost details, showing 3 metrics')
Keyboard focus order: left rail actions -> expand toggle -> detailed controls -> close (reverse on collapse)
Color tokens for positive/negative deltas must meet 4.5:1 at body size; if using accent colors add an outline or icon to convey direction
Motion preference: respect prefers-reduced-motion and use instant transitions for users who opt out
open_questions: Should the left rail quick-actions include a direct 'rollback' CTA or only a link to the rollout page?
Is there appetite to standardize sparkline library across console or allow page-specific variations?
Do we prefer tokens named motion.duration.split-rail-enter or reuse motion.duration.short?
